On October 29, 2026, Strategy Inc (the "Company") filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware four amended and restated certificates of designations: • STRF Stock : Amended and Restated Certificate of Designations of the Company's 10.00% Series A Perpetual Strife Preferred Stock (the "A&R STRF Stock CoD"); • STRC Stock : Second Amended and Restated Certificate of Designations of the Company's Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Stretch Preferred Stock (the "Second A&R STRC Stock CoD"); • STRK Stock : Amended and Restated Certificate of Designations of the Company's 8.00% Series A Perpetual Strike Preferred Stock (the "A&R STRK Stock CoD"); and • STRD Stock : Amended and Restated Certificate of Designations of the Company's 10.00% Series A Perpetual Stride Preferred Stock (the "A&R STRD Stock CoD" and, together with the A&R STRF Stock CoD, the Second A&R STRC Stock CoD and the A&R STRK Stock CoD, the "A&R CoDs"). The Second A&R STRC Stock CoD will become effective at 12:01 a.m., Eastern Time, on November 1, 2026, and the Amended Certificates of Designations for the STRF Stock, STRK Stock and STRD Stock will become effective at 12:01 a.m., Eastern Time, on January 1, 2027 (each, the "Applicable Effective Time"). Until the Applicable Effective Time, each series will continue to be governed by its applicable existing certificate of designations. Each A&R CoD provides for regular dividends to have a record date on each calendar day and to be payable (if declared) on the following Business Day (as defined in the applicable A&R CoD), together with such conforming and related changes as set forth therein. The modification does not increase or decrease the total amount of regular dividends payable on the STRF Stock, the STRC Stock, the STRK Stock or the STRD Stock, change any of STRF Stock’s, STRC Stock’s, STRK Stock’s or STRD Stock’s dividend rates, increase or decrease the Company’s overall dividend payment obligations, or, other than as it pertains to the change in the frequency of dividend payments and other related changes, change the applicable rights and protections associated with each of STRF Stock, STRC Stock, STRK Stock and STRD Stock dividends. As set forth below, the A&R CoDs were approved and adopted by the Company’s stockholders at the Company’s Special Meeting of Stockholders held on October 28, 2026 (the "Special Meeting"). Additional information regarding the A&R CoDs can be found in the Company’s definitive proxy statement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on October 5, 2026 under the heading "Proposal 1 — APPROVAL AND ADOPTION OF AN AMENDED AND RESTATED CERTIFICATE OF DESIGNATIONS FOR EACH OF THE COMPANY’S 10.00% SERIES A PERPETUAL STRIFE PREFERRED STOCK, VARIABLE RATE SERIES A PERPETUAL STRETCH PREFERRED STOCK, 8.00% SERIES A PERPETUAL STRIKE PREFERRED STOCK AND 10.00% SERIES A PERPETUAL STRIDE PREFERRED STOCK, TO PERMIT DAILY DIVIDENDS." Item 8.01 Other Events. Confirmation of STRC Stock Transition Dividends As previously disclosed in the Company's Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the SEC on October 16, 2026, the Company declared daily dividends on STRC Stock with record dates on each calendar day from November 1 through November 30, 2026 and payment date on the next Business Day following its respective record date (the "November Daily Dividends"), subject to the satisfaction of the following events (the "Contingent Dividend Condition"): • Stockholder approval of Proposal 1 at the Special Meeting at or prior to 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on October 31, 2026; and • The filing and effectiveness of the Second A&R STRC Stock CoD by 12:01 a.m., Eastern Time, on November 1, 2026. As noted above, Proposal 1 was approved by the Company's stockholders at the Special Meeting, and the Second A&R STRC Stock CoD has been filed and will become effective at 12:01 a.m., Eastern Time, on November 1, 2026. Accordingly, upon the Second A&R STRC Stock CoD’s effectiveness, the November Daily Dividends will be payable in accordance with their terms. Important Information About KPIs The Company seeks to acquire bitcoin in a manner it believes to be accretive to common stockholders. To assess achievement of this strategy, the Company monitors and reviews the following Key Performance Indicators ("KPIs"): ▪ Bitcoin Per Share (in Sats) (or BPS (in Sats) ) represents the ratio between the Company’s gross bitcoin holdings and its Assumed Diluted Shares Outstanding, expressed in terms of "Satoshis" or "Sats", where: ▪ "Assumed Diluted Shares Outstanding" refers to the aggregate of the Company’s Basic Shares Outstanding as of the dates presented plus all additional shares that would result from the assumed conversion of all outstanding convertible notes and convertible preferred stock, exercise of all outstanding stock option awards, and settlement of all outstanding restricted stock units and performance stock units as of such dates. Assumed Diluted Shares Outstanding is not calculated using the treasury method, incorporates approximate forfeitures of awards in the current period which may be subject to future adjustment and does not take into account any vesting conditions (in the case of equity awards), the exercise price of any stock option awards or any contractual conditions limiting convertibility of convertible debt instruments. ▪ "Basic Shares Outstanding" reflects the actual class A common stock and class B common stock outstanding as of the dates presented. For purposes of this calculation, outstanding shares of such stock are deemed to include shares, if any, that (A) were sold under at-the-market equity offering programs, or (B) were issued pursuant to (i) options that had been exercised, (ii) restricted stock units that have vested or (iii) conversion requests received with respect to convertible securities, but which in each case were pending issuance as of the dates presented. ▪ A "Satoshi" or a "Sat" is one one-hundred-millionth of one bitcoin, currently the smallest indivisible unit of a bitcoin. ▪ BTC Yield represents the percentage change in BPS (in Sats) over a period. It is calculated by dividing the difference in BPS between the beginning of a period and the end of a period by the BPS at the beginning of the period. For an interim Measurement Period that is part of a longer Reference Period, BTC Yield is calculated as the BTC Yield for the period from the beginning of the Reference Period to the end of the Measurement Period, less the BTC Yield for the period from the beginning of the Reference Period to the beginning of the Measurement Period. ▪ BTC Gain represents the BTC Yield for a period in gross bitcoin terms. It is calculated by multiplying the BTC Yield for that period by the Company’s gross bitcoin holdings at the beginning of a specified period. For an interim Measurement Period that is part of a longer Reference Period, BTC Gain is calculated by multiplying the BTC Yield for the Measurement Period by the Company’s gross bitcoin holdings at the beginning of the Reference Period. ▪ BTC $ Gain represents BTC Gain as an illustrative dollar value. It is calculated by multiplying the BTC Gain by the market price of bitcoin as reported on the Coinbase exchange as of the applicable measurement time. "Measurement Period" refers to the period being measured, and "Reference Period" refers to the longer period of which the Measurement Period may be a sub-part. When the Company presents these metrics for an interim period within a fiscal year (e.g., a monthly, quarterly, or quarter-to-date period), then the Measurement Period is that interim period, and unless otherwise stated, the Reference Period is the fiscal year-to-date period ending on the last day of the Measurement Period. For example, assume BPS (in Sats) is 100 at the beginning of a fiscal year, 110 at the end of the first quarter and 125 at the end of the second quarter. The BTC Yield for the second quarter is calculated as (125/100 − 1) less (110/100 − 1), or 15%. The first and second quarter BTC Yields of 10% and 15%, respectively, sum to the year-to-date BTC Yield of 25%. With 1,000 bitcoin held at the beginning of the fiscal year, BTC Gain would be 100 bitcoin (10% × 1,000) and 150 bitcoin (15% × 1,000) for the first and second quarters, respectively, which sum to the year-to-date BTC Gain of 250 bitcoin. For determining BTC $ Gain quarter to date and year to date, unless otherwise specified, the Company uses the current market price of bitcoin as reported on the Coinbase exchange as of the applicable measurement time. For determining BTC $ Gain for a past fiscal year or other past period, the Company uses the market price of bitcoin as of 4:00pm ET as reported on the Coinbase exchange on the last day of the applicable period, unless stated otherwise. These prices are used solely to facilitate these illustrative calculations. The Company uses BPS (in Sats), BTC Yield, BTC Gain and BTC $ Gain as KPIs to help assess the performance of its strategy of acquiring bitcoin in a manner it believes to be accretive to shareholders. The Company also believes these KPIs can supplement investors’ understanding of how the Company chooses to fund bitcoin purchases and the value created in a period: ▪ BPS (in Sats) provides management and investors a baseline with which to assess the Company’s achievement of its strategy of acquiring bitcoin in an accretive manner over a given period. When evaluating a capital raise transaction, the Company considers the impact the transaction will have on this metric. This metric forms the baseline for the Company’s BTC Yield, BTC Gain and BTC $ Gain KPIs, each of which presents the change in BPS (in Sats) over a period in a different format. ▪ BTC Yield helps management and investors assess the Company’s achievement of its strategy of acquiring bitcoin in an accretive manner across periods. The Company uses BTC Yield to evaluate whether its capital markets activity and bitcoin acquisition strategy have resulted in gross per-share accretion (or dilution) on an Assumed Diluted Shares Outstanding basis over an applicable period, and to compare the impact of its strategy across periods. ▪ BTC Gain helps the Company measure the accretive or dilutive impact of the change in BPS (in Sats) over an applicable period in absolute terms relative to the Company’s bitcoin holdings. This metric can be particularly helpful when comparing the execution of the Company’s capital markets strategy across periods. A larger bitcoin asset base may produce a lower BTC Yield but the same BTC Gain. For example, a 10% BTC Yield on 100,000 bitcoin and a 5% BTC Yield on 200,000 bitcoin each result in a BTC Gain of 10,000 bitcoin. ▪ BTC $ Gain further expresses the percentage change reflected in the BTC Yield metric as an illustrative dollar value by multiplying that bitcoin-denominated change by the market price of bitcoin at the end of the applicable period as described above. The Company refers to this metric for illustrative purposes to consider the magnitude of BTC Gain with reference to the market price of bitcoin. When management uses these metrics, management takes into account their various limitations. With respect to BPS (in Sats), BTC Yield, BTC Gain and BTC $ Gain, these limitations include that the metrics: ▪ do not take into account that the Company’s assets, including its bitcoin, are subject to (i) all of the Company’s existing and future liabilities, including its debt, and (ii) the preferential rights of the Company’s preferred stockholders to dividends and the Company’s assets in a liquidation, and that all such claims rank senior to those of the Company’s common equity. Therefore, holders of such excluded instruments may have claims on the Company’s assets (including bitcoin) senior to those of holders of common stock in the event of the Company’s liquidation. As a result, the additional bitcoin acquired using proceeds from the sale of such instruments may not accrete to common stockholders; and ▪ assume that all indebtedness will be refinanced or, in the case of the Company’s senior convertible debt instruments and convertible preferred stock, converted into shares of class A common stock in accordance with their respective terms. Different assumptions would produce materially different results, and these KPIs may overstate or understate the Company’s bitcoin that would remain attributable to holders of common stock after accounting for senior claims (net of the Company’s USD Assets). BPS (in Sats), BTC Yield, BTC Gain and BTC $ Gain are not, and should not be understood as, financial performance, valuation or liquidity measures. Specifically: ▪ BPS (in Sats) does not represent (i) the Company's ability to satisfy its financial obligations, or (ii) the Company’s book value per share. ▪ BTC Yield is not equivalent to "yield" in the traditional financial context. It is not a measure of the return on investment the Company’s shareholders may have achieved historically or can achieve in the future by purchasing stock of the Company. Nor is it a measure of income generated by the Company’s operations or its bitcoin holdings, return on investment on its bitcoin holdings, or any other similar financial measure of the performance of its business or assets. ▪ BTC Gain and BTC $ Gain are not equivalent to "gain" in the traditional financial context. They also are not measures of the return on investment the Company’s shareholders may have achieved historically or can achieve in the future by purchasing stock of the Company. Nor are they measures of income generated by the Company’s operations or its bitcoin holdings, return on investment on its bitcoin holdings, or any other similar financial measure of the performance of its business or assets. BTC $ Gain also does not represent a fair value gain of the Company’s bitcoin holdings nor any other realized or unrealized financial gain. BTC $ Gain may be positive during periods when the Company has incurred fair value losses on its bitcoin holdings, or negative during periods when the Company has incurred fair value gains on its bitcoin holdings. The trading price of the Company’s class A common stock is informed by numerous factors in addition to the Company’s bitcoin holdings and its actual or potential shares of common stock outstanding. As a result, the trading price of the Company’s securities can deviate significantly from the fair market value of the Company’s bitcoin. None of BPS (in Sats), BTC Yield, BTC Gain or BTC $ Gain is indicative or predictive of the trading price of the Company’s securities. Investors should rely on the financial statements and other disclosures contained in the Company’s SEC filings. In particular, the Company has adopted Accounting Standards Update No. 2023-08, Intangibles—Goodwill and Other—Crypto Assets (Subtopic 350-60): Accounting for and Disclosure of Crypto Assets ("ASU 2023-08"). ASU 2023-08 requires the Company to measure its bitcoin at fair value in its statement of financial position as of the end of a reported period, and to recognize gains and losses from changes in the fair value in net income (loss) for the reported period. As a result, the Company may incur unrealized gain or loss on digital assets based on changes in the market price of bitcoin during a period, as well as gain or loss from the sale of digital assets during a period. These gains and losses are not reflected in BPS (in Sats), BTC Yield, BTC Gain or BTC $ Gain. For example, if the Company increases its bitcoin holdings relative to Assumed Diluted Shares Outstanding during a reported period, the Company would achieve increased BPS (in Sats) and positive BTC Yield, BTC Gain and BTC $ Gain even if the Company reports significant realized or unrealized loss on digital assets for the period. Similarly, if the Company increases Assumed Diluted Shares Outstanding at a faster rate than its bitcoin holdings, then the Company would experience decreased BPS (in Sats) and negative BTC Yield, BTC Gain, and BTC $ Gain, even if the Company reports significant unrealized gain on digital assets for the period. As noted above, these KPIs are narrow in purpose and are used by management to help assess whether the Company is raising and deploying capital in a manner accretive to shareholders solely as it pertains to its bitcoin holdings. References to a transaction, or to the Company’s capital deployment, being "accretive" or "dilutive" refer only to the effect on the specified KPI under the stated assumptions. They do not mean that the transaction is accretive or dilutive to the Company’s earnings, cash flow, book value, enterprise value, intrinsic value, or the trading price of the Company’s securities. In calculating BPS (in Sats), BTC Yield, BTC Gain, and BTC $ Gain, the Company does not consider the source of capital used to acquire its bitcoin. When the Company purchases bitcoin using proceeds from offerings of non-convertible notes or non-convertible preferred stock, or convertible notes or preferred stock that carry conversion prices above the current trading price of the Company's common stock or conversion rights that are not then exercisable, such transactions have the effect of increasing the BPS (in Sats), BTC Yield, BTC Gain and BTC $ Gain, while also increasing the Company’s indebtedness and senior claims of holders of instruments other than class A common stock with respect to dividends and to the Company’s assets, including its bitcoin, if the Company were to liquidate, in a manner that is not reflected in these metrics. If any of the Company’s convertible notes mature or are redeemed without being converted into common stock, or if the Company elects to redeem or repurchase its non-convertible instruments (including certain of its perpetual preferred stock), the Company may be required to sell shares of its class A common stock or bitcoin to generate sufficient cash proceeds to satisfy those obligations, either of which would have the effect of decreasing BPS (in Sats), BTC Yield, BTC Gain and BTC $ Gain. The assumptions used in calculating these metrics do not contemplate adjustments for such decreases. Accordingly, these metrics might overstate or understate the accretive nature of the Company’s use of capital to buy bitcoin because not all bitcoin is purchased using proceeds from issuances of class A common stock, instruments that are convertible into class A common stock may be forfeited or repaid with funds other than from the sale of class A common stock in the period in question rather than being exercised for or converted into class A common stock and not all proceeds from issuances of class A common stock are used to purchase bitcoin. In addition, the Company is required to pay dividends with respect to its perpetual preferred stock in perpetuity. The Company could pay these dividends with cash or, in the case of STRK Stock, by issuing shares of class A common stock. The Company has issued shares of class A common stock and certain series of its preferred stock for cash to fund the payment of cash dividends. In the future, the Company may also issue shares of class A common stock in lieu of paying dividends on STRK Stock. As a result, the Company has experienced, and may experience in the future, increases in Assumed Diluted Shares Outstanding without corresponding increases in its bitcoin holdings, resulting in decreases in BPS (in Sats), BTC Yield, BTC Gain and BTC $ Gain for the applicable periods. The Company has historically not paid any dividends on its shares of class A common stock, and by presenting these KPIs the Company makes no suggestion that it intends to do so in the future. Holders of the Company’s securities, including its class A common stock and preferred stock, have no ownership interest in, or redemption right with respect to, the Company's bitcoin holdings. The Company determines its KPI targets based on its history and future goals. The Company’s ability to maintain any given level of BPS (in Sats), or achieve positive BTC Yield, BTC Gain, or BTC $ Gain may depend on a variety of factors, including factors outside of its control, such as the price of bitcoin, and the availability of debt and equity financing on favorable terms. Past performance is not indicative of future results, and the Company’s KPI results for any particular interim period may not be indicative of its ability to achieve longer-term objectives under its bitcoin strategy. Additionally, the Company’s KPIs may improve, and the Company may achieve its targets or objectives, even as it incurs losses or the market price of its class A common stock declines. These KPIs are merely supplements, not substitutes for the financial statements and other disclosures contained in the Company’s SEC filings. For shares traded on Nasdaq, the ex-dividend date is generally the same day as the record date, if it falls on a trading day, or the immediately preceding business day, if the record date does not fall on a trading day. docs.text: EX-99.1 2 ex99-1.htm EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR) Announces ETH Holdings Reach 6.07 Million Tokens, and Total Crypto and Total Cash & Marketable Securities Holdings of $14.3 Billion Bitmine owns 4.97% of the total ETH coin supply of 122.2 million Vitalik Buterin, founder of Ethereum, states "I’ve finally made up my mind, ETH is a store of value, ETH is money" Bitmine is 99% of the way to the ‘Alchemy of 5%’ in just 15 months Bitmine released Chairman’s Message on October 7 titled "Crypto Bull Underway — This Cycle Likely the Largest" Bitmine was added to the Russell 1000 Large-cap index on June 26, 2026 Bitmine’s Series A Preferred Stock is trading on the NYSE under the symbol BMNP Bitmine has 5,227,037 staked ETH, representing $11.7 billion at $2,234 per ETH. MAVAN (Made in America VAlidator Network) is a premier Ethereum staking destination for BMNR and institutional investors Bitmine owns $75 million of Eightco (NASDAQ: ORBS), now one of the only publicly listed equities in the world to provide investors indirect exposure to OpenAI Bitmine Crypto + Total Cash Holdings & Marketable Securities + "Moonshots" total $14.3 billion, including 6.07 million ETH tokens, total cash & marketable securities of $475 million, and other crypto holdings Bitmine remains supported by a premier group of institutional investors including ARK’s Cathie Wood, MOZAYYX, Founders Fund, Bill Miller III, Pantera, Kraken, DCG, Galaxy Digital and personal investor Thomas "Tom" Lee to support Bitmine’s goal of acquiring 5% of ETH NORWALK, CT, November 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — (NYSE: BMNR) Bitmine Immersion Technologies, Inc. ("Bitmine" or the "Company"), a Bitcoin and Ethereum Network company with a focus on the accumulation of crypto for long term investment, today announced Bitmine crypto + total cash & marketable securities + "moonshots" holdings totaling $14.3 billion. As of November 8, 2026 at 2:00pm ET, the Company’s crypto holdings are comprised of 6,070,092 ETH at $2,234 per ETH (per Coinbase NASDAQ: COIN), 216 Bitcoin (BTC), $180 million stake in Beast Industries, $75 million stake in Eightco Holdings (NASDAQ: ORBS) ("moonshots") and total cash & marketable securities of $475 million. Bitmine’s ETH holdings are 4.97% of the ETH supply (of 122.2 million ETH). "Vitalik Buterin, founder of Ethereum, declared at Devcon 8 in Mumbai, ‘I’ve finally made up my mind, ETH is a store of value, ETH is money.’ This declaration by the founder of Ethereum, in my view, is a seismic shift, clarifying how ETH will capture value in this coming supercycle of tokenization and AI," stated Thomas "Tom" Lee, Chairman of Bitmine. "In my opinion, ETH was not a ‘cash flow’ token model, like HYPE or LIT, but rather pristine and trusted collateral, and reflective of how Ethereum is the Layer 1 chosen by the vast majority of financial institutions moving assets onto the blockchain," continued Lee. Vitalik further clarified his views with a X.com post (link here) expanding on why he believes "ETH as store of value (SoV)." The 3 reasons he described: 1. ETH as fee-burning is not as strong "as it seemed;" 2. Optimizing for fee-burning is not necessarily compatible with decentralization and capture resistance; and 3. Optimizing for SoV aligns with ETH’s strengths of decentralization and CROPS. "In other words, ETH as a Store of Value is most consistent with the future roadmap of ETH and also the role ETH will play in the coming super tokenization supercycle," added Lee. Source: X.com Source: X.com "Over the past week, we acquired 9,587 ETH. Bitmine’s track record of consistent buying of crypto is unmatched by any public company in the world. Bitmine has bought ETH each week since the inception of the ETH Treasury Strategy on June 30, 2025," stated Lee. On October 7, Bitmine released its latest Chairman’s message titled "Crypto Bull Underway — This Cycle Likely the Largest." The presentation is available at the Bitmine website ( presentation link ). Earlier in 2026, Bitmine launched MAVAN (the Made in America VAlidator Network), the institutional-grade staking platform. While MAVAN was originally developed to support Bitmine’s own Ethereum treasury, MAVAN has expanded to serve institutional investors, custodians, and ecosystem partners seeking best-in-class staking infrastructure. A portion of Bitmine’s ETH is already staked on the MAVAN platform. As of November 8, 2026, Bitmine total staked ETH stands at 5,227,037 ($11.7 billion at $2,234 per ETH). "Bitmine has staked more ETH than other entities in the world. At scale (when Bitmine’s ETH is fully staked by MAVAN and its staking partners), the projected ETH staking rewards would be $359 million on an annualized basis, using BMNR’s trailing 7-day staking yield of 2.65% as of November 8, 2026. This compares to annualized staking rewards of $309 million based upon 5.2 million staked ETH (86% of the 6.07 million ETH held by Bitmine)," continued Lee. Bitmine’s crypto holdings reign as the #1 Ethereum treasury and #2 global treasury, behind Strategy Inc. (NASDAQ: MSTR), which reportedly owns 849,327 BTC valued at approximately $69 billion. Bitmine remains the largest ETH treasury in the world. Bitmine management believes the GENIUS Act and the Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) Project Crypto are as transformational to financial services in 2026 as the U.S. action on August 15, 1971, which ended the Bretton Woods system and took the U.S. dollar off the gold standard 55 years ago. This 1971 event was the catalyst for the modernization of Wall Street, creating the iconic Wall Street titans and financial and payment rails of today. The Chairman’s message can be found here: https://www.Bitminetech.io/chairmans-message The Fiscal Full Year 2025 Earnings presentation and corporate presentation can be found here: https://Bitminetech.io/investor-relations/ To stay informed, please sign up at: https://Bitminetech.io/contact-us/ About Bitmine Bitmine Immersion Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BMNR), together with its subsidiaries ("Bitmine" or the "Company"), is a blockchain technology infrastructure company operating across institutional digital asset staking and validation services, bitcoin mining, and strategic digital asset management. As the world’s leading Ethereum Treasury company, it implements an innovative digital asset strategy for institutional investors and public market participants. The Company provides institutional-grade staking and validation infrastructure—through which it earns staking rewards and validation income—alongside bitcoin mining activities. Bitmine holds digital assets strategically, generating yield on those holdings to support liquidity and capital formation. Since 2025, the Company has expanded its blockchain infrastructure capabilities, including developing and deploying MAVAN, its institutional staking and validation platform. The Company’s activities further include investments in early-stage blockchain opportunities ("moonshot" investments) and ancillary mining, hosting, and consulting services. For additional details, follow on X: https://x.com/bitmnr https://x.com/fundstrat Cautionary Note on Forward Looking Statements This press release contains statements that constitute "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended. This press release specifically contains forward-looking statements regarding: (i) the Company’s goal of acquiring 5% of the total ETH supply (the "Alchemy of 5%" initiative); (ii) the Company’s digital asset accumulation and treasury strategy, including statements regarding continued weekly ETH acquisitions and the Company’s status as the largest ETH treasury in the world; (iii) the Company’s staking operations, including projected annualized ETH staking rewards of approximately $359 million at scale and currently projected annualized staking revenues of approximately $309 million based on currently staked ETH; (iv) MAVAN’s expansion to serve institutional investors, custodians, and ecosystem partners; (v) management’s beliefs regarding crypto market conditions, including the views that a crypto bull market is underway and regarding the significance of the market reaction to the Binance theft and the resilience of the crypto industry; (vi) management’s opinion regarding the potential impact of the GENIUS Act and SEC Project Crypto on financial services; and (vii) statements regarding the value of the Company’s crypto, cash, marketable securities, and "moonshot" holdings. (Nasdaq: DFDV) (the "Company" or "DeFi Dev Corp."), the first U.S. public company with a treasury strategy built to accumulate and compound Solana ("SOL"), today announced that its total holdings of SOL and SOL equivalents increased by 8,881 SOL since its last update, bringing its treasury to approximately 2,609,829 SOL, up from 2,600,948 SOL. The increase marks the Company's ninth consecutive week of SOL purchases since September 14, 2026, building on its return to active accumulation on August 27. The continued purchases reflect the Company's continued execution of its treasury strategy, focused on growing SOL holdings and increasing SOL per share ("SPS") over time. "Our strategy remains consistent: accumulate SOL, compound our holdings, and grow SOL per share," said Joseph Onorati, Chief Executive Officer of DeFi Development Corp. "We remain focused on disciplined execution and positioning the Company to create long-term shareholder value as the Solana ecosystem continues to develop." Based on its $10.00 stated amount, CHAD's 14.00% annualized dividend rate equates to $1.40 per share annually. Dividends are cumulative and payable each business day when, as and if declared by the Company's Board of Directors. CHAD offers income-focused investors a differentiated way to participate in the Company's SOL treasury strategy. Unlike traditional corporate treasuries, which typically hold cash and other low-yielding assets, DeFi Development Corp.'s SOL holdings can generate recurring income through native staking and validator operations. The Company believes this productive treasury provides a strong foundation for scaling its digital credit offerings. "CHAD combines a 14% annualized dividend rate with a treasury of productive SOL assets, creating what we believe is a compelling proposition for income-focused investors," said Onorati. "As we grow CHAD, our objective is to expand our capacity to accumulate SOL while continuing to drive long-term SOL per share growth for common shareholders." The Company intends to continue growing CHAD as a core component of its long-term capital strategy, providing income-focused investors with an alternative to common equity while supporting continued SOL accumulation.
